- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias in next 3–5 periods.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 70–75 range after 75+), model overreacts — adjust forecast to align with recent mean.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model underestimates — increase forecast slightly to avoid missing reversal.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes in early 30d horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish — add 1–2% buffer to forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture momentum shifts — use sentiment-weighted smoothing or lagged sentiment correction.
